program.name: ndm_detectspikes
program.help:
Detect spikes on a high-pass filtered .fil file and write the shared spike-time .res files.
First, the program automatically computes a baseline 'noise' level, using a subset of the data. Then, spikes are detected whenever the signal crosses a threshold proportional to the baseline 'noise' level. To avoid spurious detections, the signal must have a local maximum (or minimum, depending on the sign of the signal) within a fixed search window starting at threshold crossing. Also, the duration between consecutive spikes must be greater than a fixed 'refractory' period.
The detection engine (method: standard, sdiff, or stderiv) and, for sdiff/stderiv, the spatial-derivative order (methodOrder) are set in the session's ndm_detectspikes program node; they are not declared here. The detection engine also produces a .spk in passing (there is no detect-only engine mode), which is discarded — ndm_extractspikes produces the waveform files from the shared .res.
PARAMETERS
# thresholdFactor
Threshold = thresholdFactor * baseline 'noise' level
# refractoryPeriod
Number of samples to skip after a spike, before trying to detect a new spike
# peakSearchLength
Length of the peak search window (in number of samples)
# start
Starting point in the file (in s) for computation of baseline 'noise' level
# duration
Duration (in s) for computation of baseline 'noise' level
# inputExtension
Extension of the data file read for detection, without the leading dot (default fil, i.e. <session>.fil). Set it to an alternative, externally-processed source (e.g. car.fil or filtered.dat) to detect from that file instead. The source must be high-pass filtered like the usual .fil; ndm_detectspikes does not filter it.
# thresholdNoise
stderiv engine only (refused for other methods): the signal the baseline noise level is measured on. sdiff (default, historical) measures the spatial derivative before the temporal first-difference, while detection thresholds the differenced signal, whose noise is smaller -- so the threshold sits above thresholdFactor * 4 sigma of the detection signal (about 1.65x on the reference session: 0.8 gives ~5.3 sigma). stderiv measures the detection signal itself, so the threshold is exactly thresholdFactor * 4 sigma, the same convention as ndm_reextractspikes_stderiv. Re-pick thresholdFactor when switching (~1.33 reproduces the historical 0.8). The run log prints the effective threshold in detection-signal sigma either way.
# recenterMode
stderiv engine only: where each detection is placed before the shared .res is written. stderiv (default, historical) = sample of maximum summed |stderiv| over the group. raw = sample of maximum negative deflection of the group-referenced raw signal (x - group mean), summed over the group in per-channel noise units -- the physical trough; stable for units whose stderiv waveform has several near-equal extrema. Applied to every spike: mixing anchors within a unit splits it into two alignments. With raw, stderiv waveforms extracted later carry their extremum a few samples before peakSampleIndex.
# recenterHalfWidth
stderiv engine only: search +-recenterHalfWidth samples around each detection (0 = no re-centring). Empty keeps the historical window, which can move a detection by more than 10 samples onto a neighbouring spike. recenterMode raw with recenterHalfWidth 8 was the best tested setting on the reference session.
# detectArms
stderiv engine only. stderiv (default) detects on the stderiv signal alone. hybrid adds a second detection pass on the group-referenced raw signal (x - group mean, no temporal difference) and merges both with the refractory rule. Each pass thresholds at thresholdFactor * 4 sigma of its own signal (implies thresholdNoise stderiv; an explicit sdiff is refused). It recovers spikes whose footprint is shared by neighbouring channels, which the spatial derivative attenuates, but also admits more multi-unit activity. Use with recenterHalfWidth below refractoryPeriod/2 so merged events cannot be re-centred onto one sample. The .res keeps the method name; the run log records the arms and per-arm counts.
# flatRunMax
stderiv engine only. Reject a detected spike if any channel of its raw window (nSamples around the re-centred position) holds more than flatRunMax identical consecutive samples -- zero-filled gaps (e.g. a back-filled DAC ring-buffer overrun) or a stuck line. 0 or unset = off. Check the data first: a median-high-passed .fil (ndm_hipass) is exactly 0 wherever the centre sample is the window median, giving short zero runs (up to ~17 samples) at sign changes and on spike downstrokes; 5 removes 31% of spikes on the reference chunk, ~20 keeps them and still catches dropouts.
# dedupSamples
stderiv engine only. After re-centring, drop a spike positioned within dedupSamples samples of the previous kept spike of its group; the earlier one is kept. Unset = 0 (identical positions only -- re-centring collapses a few pairs onto one sample); -1 = off.
METHOD TOKENS
The method may be qualified so the transform is stated in the artifact name rather than inferred: stderiv_S<order> runs the plain spatial derivative (orders 1-3) and leaves any per-group sdiffPairs unused, while stderiv_C<order> applies the session's sdiffPairs pattern -- order 4 for a single-partner pattern, order 5 for a reference-set pattern (one written with '+'). Outputs are stamped with the full token, e.g. <session>.spk.stderiv_C4.<group>.
Orders 4 and 5 are derived from the pattern itself and cannot be requested through methodOrder; a plain "stderiv" keeps the historical behaviour of applying whatever sdiffPairs the groups define.
